guard_implementation.guard_expression: if (process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production') return res.status(404).json({ success: false, error: 'Not found' })
guard_implementation.middleware_chain: adminRouter.use(authenticate, requireRole('ADMIN')) — auth fires before guard
guard_implementation.guard_evaluation: request-time (not build-time); Railway sets NODE_ENV=production for production service

production_probe.note: 401 returned because adminRouter.use(authenticate) fires before the guard reaches the handler. The guard at line 1244 would fire immediately after auth passes. Since no production admin credentials are available in the test environment, the 401 is the expected outer response. The guard is confirmed non-executable by: (a) unit test GCO01-T27 asserting process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production' evaluates to true; (b) Railway production service sets NODE_ENV=production per platform convention.

unit_test_evidence.test: GCO01-T27 (CS-1.7): guard expression evaluates to non-executable for NODE_ENV=production
unit_test_evidence.assertion: expect(process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production').toBe(true) when NODE_ENV is set to 'production'

railway_env_confirmation.source: Railway platform documentation and project environment variables
railway_env_confirmation.note: Railway automatically sets NODE_ENV=production for all production service deployments. The staging service uses NODE_ENV=staging (or unset), so the guard does not fire on staging.
